message.content:
Here’s a balanced leg‑workout routine that targets all major muscle groups (quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves) and includes both strength and mobility components:

| Exercise | Primary Muscles | How to Do It | Sets × Reps |
|----------|-----------------|--------------|-------------|
| **Squats** (bodyweight or barbell) | Quads, glutes, hamstrings, core | Feet shoulder‑width apart, back straight, lower until thighs parallel or below; push through heels to stand. | 3–4 × 8–12 |
| **Lunges** (forward or reverse) | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Step forward (or backward) into a lunge, keeping torso upright; alternate legs. | 3 × 10–12 per leg |
| **Deadlifts** (Romanian or conventional) | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back | Keep back neutral, hinge at hips, lift barbell while keeping it close to shins. | 3–4 × 6–10 |
| **Step‑ups** (onto a bench or box) | Quads, glutes | Step onto platform with one foot, drive through heel to lift body; alternate legs. | 3 × 10–12 per leg |
| **Calf Raises** (standing or seated) | Calves | Raise heels off floor, hold briefly, lower slowly. | 4 × 12–15 |
| **Hip Thrusts** | Glutes, hamstrings | Back on bench, barbell over hips, thrust upward, squeeze glutes at top. | 3–4 × 8–12 |
| **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Push weighted platform away from you, keeping knees at ~90° angle. | 3 × 10–12 |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | One foot behind on bench, squat down with front leg. | 3 × 8–10 per leg |
| **Glute Bridge March** | Glutes, hamstrings | Bridge position, lift one knee toward chest, alternate. | 3 × 12–15 per side |
| **Bodyweight Glute Kickbacks** | Glutes | On all fours, kick one leg back and up, keeping knee bent. | 3 × 12–15 per leg |

### Warm‑up (5–10 min)
- Light cardio (jog, bike, jump rope)
- Dynamic stretches: leg swings, hip circles, walking lunges

### Cool‑down (5–10 min)
- Static stretches: quad stretch, hamstring stretch, calf stretch, hip flexor stretch
- Foam rolling or myofascial release on quads, hamstrings, calves

### Tips
- **Progressive overload:** Add weight or reps gradually to keep challenging muscles.
- **Form first:** Use mirrors or a trainer to ensure proper technique, especially for squats and deadlifts.
- **Recovery:** Allow 48 h between intense leg sessions; consider light activity or mobility work on rest days.

Feel free to mix and match these moves based on your goals (strength, hypertrophy, endurance) and equipment availability. Happy training!
